title: The school district’s “other pay” and BART’s overtime, back to 2015
question: Were the school district’s large “other pay” and BART’s high overtime already there before 2019?
finding: Yes for the school district: other pay was 25.5% of regular pay in 2015, rank 1 of 16 California districts with 5,000 or more paid positions (middle 5.4%), and 27.0% in 2018, rank 1 of 14. BART’s overtime as a share of regular pay by year: 2015 16.8%, 2016 17.3%, 2017 16.8%, 2018 19.4%, 2019 19.4%, 2020 12.4%, 2021 14.8%, 2022 20.5%, 2023 17.3%, 2024 16.2%, 2025 17.6%.
how: State Controller raw exports 2015-2025 (the district is missing from some later files). Other pay is the export’s own column; districts are those with 5,000 or more paid positions that year. BART is the San Francisco Bay Area Rapid Transit District as a special district.
limits: Districts book stipends, extra duty, summer school and locally funded supplements differently, so “other pay” is not like for like; the export does not say what it is. BART runs 24-hour maintenance and is short of operators in some years; overtime is not proof of abuse. Neither body is paid by the City.
